summary:
7 research items across 4 banks/strategists this window (from 60 tweets scanned, 4-day lookback) — thin research signal against the intraday chart noise dropped.

Goldman led with 3 items via @MikeZaccardi: gold-fund inflows picking up after a soft year, Taiwan-focused ETF flows turning negative for the first time in 4 months, and a retail-sales miss pulling Q3 GDP tracking down to +2.2%.

BofA contributed 2 items: Hartnett's view that GOP midterm wins could spark a market surge, and a household-balance-sheet note (via @LanceRoberts) showing savings/checking balances still well above 2019 levels.

Apollo (Slok) flagged AI-related issuance now near 40% of longer-duration IG bond supply; JPM's equity strategy desk noted momentum stocks now trade cheaper than the market on forward P/E.

No duplicate/reposted charts found this cycle; no Neil Sethi (@neilksethi / @neilksethinew) activity appeared in this window.

By bank: Goldman 3, BofA 2, Apollo/Slok 1, JPM 1.

items.author: LanceRoberts
items.text:
According to BofA, households remain in fairly solid shape with household savings and checking balances stable and up significantly from 2019.  Furthermore, there is no evidence of strain depleting the reserves. 
In other words, the lower-leg of the "K" may be smaller than the media portrays.
h/t @SoberLook @adamtaggart
